SIKASIL®-670 FIRE: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikasil®-670 Fire, January 2026, Version 06.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/sikasil_-670_fire.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikasil®-670 Fire where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (January 2026, Version 06.01).
1.2 Product description. Sikasil®-670 Fire is a fire-rated, one-part, moisture curing, low-modulus elastic joint sealant.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikasil®-670 Fire is designed for fire rated movement and connection joints on porous and non-porous substrates for interior and exterior applications.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.10.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikasil®-670 Fire
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: FIRE RATED SILICONE JOINT SEALANT
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Sustainability.
    - Contributes towards satisfying Indoor Environmental Quality (EQ) Credit: Low-Emitting Materials under LEED® v4 — 1–3 points
    - Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) in accordance with EN 15804. EPD independently verified by Institut für Bauen und Umwelt e.V. (IBU)
2.3 Certificates and test reports.
    - AS 1530.4:2014 and AS 4072.1:2005 (R2016) Fire assessment report
    - DoP Sikasil®-670 Fire – EAD 350141-00-1106:2017 – 56464597 – en
    - Fire Testing EN 13501-1, Sikasil-670 Fire, CSTB, Report No RA15-0053
    - UL Product iQ, XHBN.HW-S-0114 - Joint Systems, System No. HW-S-0114
    - CE marking and declaration of performance based on EN 15651-1:2012 Sealants for non-structural use in joints in buildings and pedestrian walkways — Part 1: Sealants for facade elements
    - CE marking and declaration of performance based on EN 15651-2:2012 Sealants for non-structural use in joints in buildings and pedestrian walkways — Part 2: Sealants for glazing
    - CE marking and declaration of performance based on EN 15651-4:2012 Sealants for non-structural use in joints in buildings and pedestrian walkways — Part 4: Sealants for pedestrian walkways
    - Airborn Sound Transmission EN 140-3, Sikasil-670 Fire, UKAS, Report No C/20664/R
2.4 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - AS 1530.4: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Features (p.1).
    - EN 1366-4: cited elsewhere in the data sheet; test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Features (p.1); Technical Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - ASTM C 719: cited elsewhere in the data sheet. Where: Features (p.1).
    - EN 15804: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Sustainability (p.1).
    - AS 1530.4:2014: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - AS 4072.1:2005: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EAD 350141-00-1106:2017: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 13501-1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards; test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1); Technical Information > Reaction to fire (p.2).
    - EN 15651-1:2012: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 15651-2:2012: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 15651-4:2012: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - EN 140-3: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Certificates And Test Reports (p.1).
    - ISO 1183-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - EN 15651-1: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Product declaration (p.2).
    - EN 15651-2: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Product declaration (p.2).
    - EN 15651-4: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Product declaration (p.2).
    - ISO 11600: cited with a stated property or value. Where: Product Information > Product declaration (p.2).
    - EN ISO 868: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore A hardness (p.2).
    - ISO 8339: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Secant tensile modulus (p.2).
    - EN ISO 7389: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Elastic recovery (p.2).
    - EN ISO 9047: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - ASTM C719: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Movement capability (p.2).
    - EN ISO 7390: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Application Information > Sag flow (p.2).
    - CQP019-1: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Skinning time (p.2).
    - CQP019-2: Sika internal procedure reference, not a published standard. Where: Application Information > Tooling time (p.2).
2.5 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Up to 4 hours fire resistance according to AS 1530.4 depending on the configuration
    - Up to 4 hours fire resistance according to EN 1366-4 depending on the configuration
    - 25 LM sealant, maintain up to 25 % lateral movement capability during fire testing
    - Movement capability of ± 35% (ASTM C 719)
    - Good adhesion to many different substrates
    - Very good resistance to weathering
    - Neutral curing
2.6 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Neutral cure silicone
    - Colour: Grey
    - Density: 1.35 kg/L (ISO 1183-1)
2.7 Product declaration.
    | EN 15651-1 | F EXT-INT CC 25 LM |
    | EN 15651-2 | G CC 25 LM |
    | EN 15651-4 | PW INT CC 25 LM |
    | ISO 11600 | F 25 LM |
    | G 25 LM |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.8 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Shore A hardness: 20 (after 28 days) (EN ISO 868)
    - Tensile strain at break: 650 % (ISO 37)
    - Elastic recovery: 70 % (EN ISO 7389)
    - Movement capability: ± 25 %; ± 35 %; ± 25 % (EN ISO 9047) (ASTM C719) (EN 1366-4)
    - Reaction to fire: Class B -s2, d0 (EN 13501-1)
    - Resistance to fire: Refer to the section 'Certificates and test reports' or contact Sika Technical Services for specific information.
    - Airborne sound insulation: Rw(C;Ctr) = 38(-2;-9)
2.9 Secant tensile modulus.
    | 100 % elongation at +23 °C | 0.30 N/mm² |
    | 100 % elongation at −20 °C | 0.50 N/mm² |
    Test method printed: (ISO 8339)
2.10 Service temperature.
    | Maximum | +150 °C |
    | Minimum | -40 °C |
2.11 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: Sikasil®-670 Fire has a shelf life of 12 months from the date of production, if it is stored in undamaged, original, sealed packaging, and if the storage conditions are met.
2.12 Packaging.
    | 300 ml cartridge | 12 cartridges per box |
    | 600 ml cylindrical foil pack | 12 foil packs per box |
2.13 Storage conditions. The Product must be stored in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +25 °C. Always refer to the packaging. Refer to the current Safety Data Sheet for information on safe handling and storage.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (January 2026, Version 06.01) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (January 2026, Version 06.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Backing material: Use closed cell, polyethylene foam backing rod.
4.3 Sag flow.
    | 20 mm profile, +50 °C | 2 mm |
    Test method printed: (EN ISO 7390)
4.4 Skinning time.
    | +23 °C and 50 % r.h. | 25 minutes |
    Test method printed: (CQP019-1)
4.5 Tooling time.
    | +23 °C and 50 % r.h. | 20 minutes |
    Test method printed: (CQP019-2)
4.6 Important.
    - Poor adhesion due to incorrect priming procedure Incorrectly defined or uncontrolled priming procedures may lead to a variation in product performance. 1. Test adhesion on project-specific substrates and agree on procedures with all parties before full project application. For more information contact Sika Technical Services.
    - Poor adhesion due to inadequate surface preparation Note: Primers are adhesion promoters. Primers cannot replace proper surface preparation and surface cleaning. 1. Do not use primers for improving poorly prepared or poorly cleaned joint surfaces.
    - The substrate must be sound, clean, dry and free of contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, cement laitance, sealant residues and poorly bonded coatings which could affect adhesion of the primer and sealant.
    - The substrate must be of sufficient strength to withstand the stress induced by the sealant during movement. Use techniques such as wire brushing, grinding, grit blasting or other suitable mechanical methods to remove all weak substrate material. Repair all damaged joint edges with suitable Sika repair products. Remove dust, loose and friable material from all surfaces before applying the sealant.
    - If tested or supported by experience, the Product can be used without primers or activators on many substrates.
4.7 Important.
    - Strictly follow installation procedures
    - Strictly follow installation procedures as defined in Method Statements, application manuals and working instructions which must always be adjusted to the actual site conditions.
    - Masking
    - It is recommended to use masking tape where neat or exact joint lines are required. Remove the tape within the skin time after finishing.
4.8 Important - Joint Backing.
    - After the required substrate preparation, insert a suitable backing rod to the required depth.
    - Priming
    - If required, prime the joint surfaces as recommended in substrate preparation. Avoid excessive application of primer causing puddles at the base of the joint. Application
    - Prepare the end of the cartridge / foil pack before or after inserting into the sealant gun. Fit the nozzle and cut it to the desired bead size. Extrude Sikasil®-670 Fire into the joint ensuring that it comes into full contact with the sides of the joint and avoiding any air entrapment.
    - Finishing
    - As soon as possible after application, sealant must be firmly tooled against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion and a smooth finish. Use a compatible tooling agent (e.g. Sika® Tooling Agent N) to smooth the joint surface. Do not use tooling products containing solvents.
4.9 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika® Remover-208 immediately after use. Once cured, hardened material can only be removed mechanically. For cleaning skin use Sika® Cleaner-350H.
4.10 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Sikasil®-670 Fire cannot be overpainted.
    - Colour variations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with the colour shade white). A change in colour is purely of aesthetic and does not adversely affect the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - Do not use Sikasil®-670 Fire on natural, cast and reconstituted stone as plasticiser migration may occur.
    - Do not use Sikasil®-670 Fire on bituminous substrates, natural rubber, EPDM rubber or on any building materials which might bleed oils, plasticizers or solvents that could degrade the sealant and cause the product to become tacky.
    - Do not use Sikasil®-670 Fire to seal joints in and around swimming pools.
    - Do not use Sikasil®-670 Fire for joints under water pressure or for permanent water immersion.
    - Do not expose Sikasil®-670 Fire to alcohol containing products during curing period.
    - Air humidity is required for the product to cure. Do not use the product in a totally confined space.
    - Changing ambient conditions can affect product performance. Skin formation and curing time can be significantly delayed by low humidity, low temperature and large joint dimensions.
4.11 Further documentation.
    - Brochure Sika Fire Stopping Solutions
    - Safety Data Sheet (SDS)

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Material temperature.
    | Maximum | +40 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
5.3 Ambient air temperature.
    | Maximum | +40 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
5.4 Substrate temperature.
    | Maximum | +40 °C |
    | Minimum | +5 °C |
    The substrate temperature must be +3 °C above dew point temperature and free from frost and ice.
5.5 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.10):
    - Colour variations may occur due to exposure to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with the colour shade white). A change in colour is purely of aesthetic and does not adversely affect the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - Air humidity is required for the product to cure. Do not use the product in a totally confined space.
    - Changing ambient conditions can affect product performance. Skin formation and curing time can be significantly delayed by low humidity, low temperature and large joint dimensions.
5.6 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: 1.35 kg/L (ISO 1183-1)
    - Shore A hardness: 20 (after 28 days) (EN ISO 868)
    - Secant tensile modulus: 100 % elongation at +23 °C | 0.30 N/mm²; 100 % elongation at −20 °C | 0.50 N/mm² (ISO 8339)
    - Tensile strain at break: 650 % (ISO 37)
    - Elastic recovery: 70 % (EN ISO 7389)
    - Movement capability: ± 25 %; ± 35 %; ± 25 % (EN ISO 9047) (ASTM C719) (EN 1366-4)
    - Reaction to fire: Class B -s2, d0 (EN 13501-1)
    - Sag flow: 20 mm profile, +50 °C | 2 mm (EN ISO 7390)
    - Skinning time: +23 °C and 50 % r.h. | 25 minutes (CQP019-1)
    - Tooling time: +23 °C and 50 % r.h. | 20 minutes (CQP019-2)
5.7 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.8 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikasil®-670 Fire, January 2026, Version 06.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/sikasil_-670_fire.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikasil 670 Fire, version 09/04/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/MSDS%20Sikasil-670%20Fire%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikasil®-670 Fire, version 21/07/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/u/sds-sikasil-670fire.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
